title: Sierra Leone - Economic Diversification Project : The Inspection Panel Notice of Non-Registration on a Request for Inspection
text:
IBRAHIM PAM
Chairperson
The Inspection Panel
 IPN REQUEST 26/01

 April 6, 2026

 MEMORANDUM TO THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTORS AND ALTERNATES
 INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION

 The Inspection Panel

 Notice of Non-Registration on a Request for Inspection

 Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone Economic Diversification Project (P164212)

  Summary

  1. In accordance with paragraph 18 of the Resolution of the World Bank Accountability
  Mechanism: Inspection Panel and Dispute Resolution Service (the “Resolution”)1, I hereby inform
  you that on February 11, 2026, the Inspection Panel( the “Panel”) received a Request for Inspection
  (the “Request”) related to the Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone Economic Diversification Project
  (P164212) ( the “Project”).

  2. The Request was submitted by two individuals from Freetown, Sierra Leone. The
  Requesters asked not to disclose their identities for fear of retaliation for submitting the Request
  with the Panel. The Request alleges that the Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Land, Tourism and other
  government Agencies supported by the military and paramilitary police demolished their two-
  bedroom house and the foundation of a five-bedroom house they were constructing in their
  property in the Bathurst Village in Western Area Rural District of Greater Freetown, Sierra Leone.
  The Request states that, according to a press release from the Ministry of Tourism, the demolitions
  took place to protect the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, where an Innovation Centre, a
  Botanical Garden, and a mini cinema for educational purposes are being constructed. According
  to the Request, the demolition of their properties was not preceded by resettlement procedures and,
  therefore, the Project violated the World Bank’s policies. A redacted copy of the Request for
  Inspection is attached as Annex I.

  3. The Panel acknowledges the seriousness of the concerns raised in the Request. The Panel’s
  initial due diligence concluded that the Request did not meet one of the criteria for registration, as
  the concerns raised in the Request at the time of its receipt are not related to the Bank-financed
  Project. I am therefore notifying you that the Panel is not registering this Request.




  1
 The World Bank Accountability Mechanism: Inspection Panel and Dispute Resolution Service, Resolution No.
  IBRD 2025-0001 and Resolution No. IDA 2025-0001 (March 7, 2025) (the “Resolution”).
 The Project

4. The Sierra Leone Economic Diversification Project was approved on July 28, 2020, for an
IDA grant of US$ 40 million equivalent. The Project’s Implementing Agencies include the
Ministry of Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Finance, and the Ministry of Tourism and Cultural
Affairs. The current closing date of the Project is April 30, 2026.

5. The Project Development Objective is “to increase investment, Small and Medium
Enterprise (SME) growth, and entrepreneurship in non-mining productive sectors in the
Recipient’s territory.”2 The Project has four components: i) improving business environment and
capacity building; ii) assisting Small and Medium Entreprises and entrepreneurship growth; iii)
Project management and evaluation; and iv) contingent emergency response component (CERC).
At the time of approval, the Project was classified as E&S Category B and the following
Operational Policies applied: Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01); Natural Habitats (OP/BP
4.04); Physical Cultural Resources (OP/BP 4.36); Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12).3 At the
time of receipt of the Request, 81 percent of Project funds had been disbursed.

The Request

6. The Request alleges that on February 26, 2025, the Project - “supported by truckloads of
heavily armed military and para-military police” - demolished the Requesters’ two-bedroom house
and the foundation of a five-bedroom house which was under construction in Bathurst Village in
Freetown, Sierra Leone. The Requesters state that they have ownership of the land where the
structures were demolished. According to the Requesters, the demolition occurred without “prior
resettlement procedures”, including stakeholder engagement, and compensation, as required under
applicable World Bank policies. The Requesters claim that the demolition which allegedly
violated the Bank policies was published on the website of the Ministry of Tourism, and which
stated that the demolitions occurred “to protect the Tacaguma Chimpanzee Sanctuary”, where an
Innovation Centre, a Botanical Garden and a mini-cinema for educational purposes are being built.
The Requesters claim that the press release was later retracted from the Ministry of Tourism
website. The Request also claims that the Project failed to follow its Grievance Mechanism
Process.

7. The Request further notes that following the destruction of the property, the Ministry of
Lands and Country Planning issued a notice inviting individuals with proof of their ownership of
land to report to the Acting Professional Head and Director of Surveys on Land for further
verification.

Panel’s Observation and Determination

8. In accordance with the Panel’s Operating Procedures 4 and following its review of
information gathered through its due diligence, the Panel confirms that the Request does not meet
one of the admissibility criteria for Registration. The Panel determines that the Request isnot

2
  Sierra Leone Economic Diversification Project, Project Appraisal Document (PAD), p.20, para. 33.
3
  PAD, p. 4, para. 140.
4
  Inspection Panel Operating Procedures (November 2025).


 2
 frivolous, absurd, or anonymous. The Panel also confirms that the Request was submitted by two
individuals from the Borrower’s territory who claim to be affected by the Project. The Panel further
notes that, at the time of submission of the Request, the Project was 81 percent disbursed. The
Panel notes that the subject matter of the Request does not concern issues of procurement, and the
Panel has not previously made a recommendation on the issue raised.

9. The Panel met with the Requesters on February 17 and March 24, 2026. During these
meetings, the Requesters reiterated their concerns as originally raised in the Request, specifically
that the Project failed to apply the Bank Policy on Involuntary Resettlement, and that its
implementation directly resulted in the unlawful destruction of their properties without
consultation or compensation. Regarding the demolitions, the Requesters told the Panel that the
Government of Sierra Leone had called on the public to submit evidence of ownership of the
properties that were demolished as the basis for compensation. The Requesters complied with this
request but received no response from the Government regarding compensation for the destruction
of their properties. The Panel also sought clarification from the Requesters regarding the location
of their properties in relation to the Project. The Requesters (in the discussion held on March 24,
2026) confirmed that their properties lie outside the Project boundaries. They further informed the
Panel that they had relied on a press release issued by the Ministry of Tourism, which stated that
the demolitions were carried out to "protect the World Bank investment" in the Tacugama
Chimpanzee Visitor Center.

10. On March 13, 2026, the Panel met with Bank Management to hear their views on the issues
raised in the Request for Inspection. Management stated that the Project includes public
investments in local infrastructure and public facilities to establish the Tacugama Innovation
Center (“Center”) and two other facilities. According to Management, the Center, which is located
in the Western Area Peninsula National Park, includes the upgrading of a 1.4 km access road, two
visitor car parks and the construction of the Center, as well as outdoor and supporting facilities,
such as a rainwater harvesting system, an amphitheater, a greenhouse and botanical garden, and a
ticket house. The total investment of the Center is $7.9 million. Management stated that the access
road has been 100% completed and the innovation center is 75% complete.

11. According to Management, the ESIA for the Project defines the geographical area of
influence as the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, the access road and the associated facilities
within the protected forest of the Western Area Peninsula Park, and there are no communities
within the forest. Management stated that the Project has an active grievance redress mechanism
which has not received any complaints related to demolitions in Bathurst Village. Management
stated that the Project is implemented entirely in a State-owned protected area where there are no
communities present. Therefore, no land acquisition was required for this Project.

12. Management informed the Panel that a Bank team conducted a field visit on June 12, 2025,
followed by a virtual meeting with the Requesters. Management stated that the Requesters agreed
their property was outside the Project area, though they asked for the Bank's assistance in resolving
their grievances with the Government. Management further added that the Government of Sierra
Leone confirmed that the demolition campaign in Bathurst Village was its own initiative to protect
the water catchment area and was unrelated to the Project.




 3
 13. The Panel reviewed the Project’s Environment and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA)
prepared for the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary and relevant project maps, and notes that the
ESIA for the Project states that the Project covers a land area of 6 ha and is located on an easily
visible and accessible site in Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary. 5 The ESIA defines the
geographical area of influence of the Project as the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary which is
within the Western Area Peninsular National Park. It also states that no land acquisition was
required as the Project is on a state land (protected forest). According to the Panel’s Resolution,6
the Panel shall accept Requests where the affected party demonstrates “that its rights or interests have
been or are likely to be directly affected by an action or omission of the Bank policies financed by the Bank
provided in all cases that such failure has had, or threatens to have, a material adverse effect.” The Panel
determines that the Requesters property is located outside the Project area and does not relate to
the Bank-financed Project or its related activities.

14. Following conversations with the Requesters on February 17 and March 24, 2026, as well
as with Bank Management on March 13, 2026, and based on a review of the Project’s ESIA and
Project documents, the Panel considers that the issues raised in the Request are not related to the
Bank Project as required by paragraph 14(b) of the Panel’s Operating Procedures. Based on
paragraph 18 of the Resolution, I therefore notify you that the Panel is not registering this Request.

 Yours sincerely,




 Ibrahim Pam

Attachment

Copy to:
Mr. Ajay Banga, President, International Bank for Reconstruction and Development

Mr. Ousmane Diagana, Regional Vice President, AFWVP

Requesters (Confidential)

  Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Enhancing Visitors’ Experience and Education at Tacugama
Chimpanzee Sanctuary, p 46, para 6.2.
6
  The Resolution, p. 3, para. 13, “The affected party must demonstrate that its rights or interests have been or are
likely to be directly affected by an action or omission of the Bank as a result of a failure of the Bank to follow its
operational policies and procedures with respect to the design, appraisal and/or implementation of a project1
financed by the Bank (including situations where the Bank is alleged to have failed in its follow-up on the borrower’s
obligations under loan agreements with respect to such policies and procedures) provided in all cases that such
failure has had, or threatens to have, a material adverse effect.”

  Annex I

 GOVERNMENT OF SIERRA LEONE


 Sierra Leone Economic Diversification Project’s Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM)
 The Sierra Leone Economic Diversification Project (SLEDP) Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) has been
 designed to address project grievances that may be raised by affected persons or community members regarding
 specific project activities, environmental and social performance, the engagement process, and/or unanticipated
 social impacts resulting from project activities.

 Objectives of GRM
 1. Establish a prompt, easy to understand, consistent and respectful mechanism to support the receiving,
 investigating, and responding to complaints or grievances arising from, and during SLEDP implementation.
 2. Ensure transparency and accountability throughout the implementation of the project amongst the relevant
 stakeholders including project beneficiaries.
 3. Resolve any emerging environmental and social grievances in project areas.
 4. To promote relations between the project implementers, executers, and beneficiaries.

 Scope of the GRM
 The SLEDP’s GRM will primarily handle issues that emerge from the implementation of project activities, such
 ` as:
 a) Inter-community dispute: Implementation of project may have direct impact or indirect on the lives and
 property of the people.
 b) Grievance among community stakeholders over ownership and participation in project activities.
 c) Grievances arising from construction work
 d) Grievance due to selection and participation of beneficiaries in project activities.
 e) Service delivery grievances
 f) Grievances due to Gender Based Violence: sexual harassment, exploitation, abuse of women and girls in
 project communities.
 h) Grievances related to land acquisition and compensation etc.


 How to file a complaint?
 Aggrieved persons can file complaint either in person, online or via telephone.

 In-Person Submission:
 Complaints and incidents may be submitted to the GRM Focal Point/Social Safeguards Specialist at 35 Percival
 Street, Freetown, by a personal visit on any of the working days (Monday-Friday) from 8:30 am- 4:00 pm. or
 telephone +23274271989 which would also be available during work hours from 8:30 am- 4:00 pm.

 Online Submission: For online submission, those who are interested can submit their complaints through the
 SLEDP website: www.sledp.gov.sl OR Email: safeguards@sledp.info or through WhatsApp on
 +23274271989.
